test_title: SSC MTS 2023 Official Paper (Held On: 06 Sept, 2023 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: What is the primary purpose of microfinance institutions (MFIs) in India?

options.text: To promote consumer spending among middle-class households
To offer financial services exclusively to large businesses
To provide small loans to low-income individuals
To facilitate foreign investment in the Indian economy

solution:
The correct answer is __**to provide small loans to low-income individuals**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Microfinance institutions (MFIs)** primarily aim to provide **small loans** to low-income individuals who do not have access to traditional banking services.
 
• These institutions play a crucial role in **financial inclusion** by offering credit to those who are typically excluded from the formal financial system.
 
• MFIs help in empowering **economically disadvantaged groups**, especially women, by providing them with the necessary capital to start or expand small businesses.
 
• They contribute to **poverty alleviation** and promote **entrepreneurship** at the grassroots level.
 
• MFIs also offer other financial services such as savings, insurance, and remittance services to their clients.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Microfinance in India has its roots in the **Self-Help Group (SHG)** movement, which started in the 1980s.
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** regulates MFIs to ensure they operate within a framework that protects the interests of borrowers.
 
• MFIs operate under various models, including the **Grameen model** and the **Self-Help Group (SHG) model**.
 
• The growth of the microfinance sector in India has led to the establishment of several **Microfinance Institutions Network (MFIN)** and **Sa-Dhan**, which are industry associations that promote best practices and advocate for the sector.
 
• Despite the benefits, the microfinance sector has faced challenges such as high-interest rates, over-indebtedness, and issues related to loan recovery practices.
